## User-authorized autonomous recovery

The person explicitly requested finishing DM-761, fixing elapsed-time hard-stop instructions, keeping the timer-policy agent working, and notifying them after both code changes are merged and pushed to main. This authorizes named-card relaunch and delivery, not self-approval or weaker verification. Attempt 8 continues the diagnosed work; historical failures are retained, not erased by a new claim.

Recovered evidence: existing attached screenshots im_01m7v6fgwe0415a0ac35zvq82q and im_01m7v6fn5a6asm2qj801ktaee2 were retrieved and independently opened. They show installed v0.48.0, DM-793 with a Play control and FAILED attempt #1: the reported problem is an unclear label rather than an absent control. The earlier claim that original-symptom evidence was unavailable was an incomplete evidence search, not a genuine blocker.

Execution instructions required for this recovery:
1. Five-/ten-minute timers are progress/stall alerts, never failure or decomposition solely for elapsed time. Productive work continues on its current claim; record evidence, current operation, expected next result and actual blockers.
2. A failed check starts diagnosis and recovery, not automatic escalation. Preserve failure logs; fix an established cause and validate changed conditions. Never blind rerun, suppress checks or claim a pass from a timeout.
3. Inspect existing card messages, attachments and commits before rediscovering or duplicating finished work.
4. Resolve known runtime/tool prerequisites automatically (existing pinned Node/npm here). Hand delegated workers the exact CLI, whole packet, role guide, source ownership and recovered evidence.
5. Coordinate shared-tree owners and a serial heavy-check slot. Never run full tests and coverage concurrently or mistake another worker's red-test phase for a completed-tree regression.
6. Keep verification and review honest; escalate only an actual unresolved scope/authority/safety/dependency decision, not a recoverable command failure. Report completed review/delivery when verified.

DM-855 already owns the timer policy change; its owner was asked to continue and coordinate final integration, rather than creating a duplicate policy convention. DM-761 worker owns focused Retry evidence and delivery-cause investigation. No repeated broad suite launched pending owner coordination. User-authorized push remains gated on verified integration; card approval remains human-only.
